title: Peak preservation strategy — regional safety bands and buffer sizing (Nov 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Provide a practical, workload-aware framing for regional headroom (tokens/sec and QPS) and a small set of safety bands we can operationalize for the Hosted/edge public endpoints. This sheet decomposes traffic by workload class, produces per-region targets, and proposes minimal prewarm/autoscale knobs to achieve a 99th–99.9th percentile preservation SLA for customer-facing endpoints.

Summary / key findings:
- Baseline 95th percentile peak (observed windowed metrics across Jul–Oct 2026): 1.65M tokens/sec global, ~22.8k QPS aggregate (short+chat requests).
- Recommended global safety band: baseline * 1.45 for 5–15min microbursts, and baseline * 2.0 for sustained 1–3 hour stress windows (business continuity target).
- Regional allocation should be asymmetric: us-west1 (35% baseline), us-east1 (30%), eu-west1 (20%), asia-east1 (15%). Apply per-region +35% microburst band and +100% sustained band before invoking cross-region fallback.
- GPU mapping: reserve H100 slices for chat/high-seq workloads, A100 for medium-length completions, and L4 for embedding-heavy/low-latency requests. Prefer cold-swap of A100->H100 only for sustained growth windows.
- Prewarm heuristics: trigger prewarm at 80% of microburst band sustained for 90s; ramp target = additional 20% of regional pool.

Assumptions and input data used:
- Average tokens per request by workload class (internal telemetry):
  - chat (context+reply): 420 tokens/req
  - short completion (single-turn): 48 tokens/req
  - embeddings (batch): 1,200 tokens-equivalent per embedding call (normalization for unit economics)
  - streaming (progressive output): counted as tokens/sec directly, typical 60 tokens/sec per stream
- Observed median request concurrency to token conversion: 1 request ~= 78 tokens/sec average (weighted by mix above).
- Typical GPU throughput (serving profiles, 8k context):
  - H100-80GB slice: ~95k tokens/sec sustained for chat-like mix (1 slice)
  - A100-40GB slice: ~48k tokens/sec sustained for mixed completions
  - L4-48GB: ~160k tokens/sec for embedding-dominant batches (batching efficiency)
- Cost delta for prewarm (per region, per hour): H100 slice ~= $23/hr, A100 slice ~= $11/hr, L4 slice ~= $4/hr (reserved pricing approximation).

Workload decomposition (global baseline numbers used to define regional splits):
- Global baseline tokens/sec (95th observed): 1,650,000 tokens/sec
- Breakdown by class (approx): chat 58% (957k t/s), short completion 24% (396k t/s), embeddings 12% (198k t/s), streaming 6% (99k t/s)

Regional baseline allocation (95th pct) and recommended bands:
Region, baseline t/s, microburst band (x1.45), sustained band (x2.0), recommended prewarm headroom t/s
us-west1, 577,500, 837,875, 1,155,000, prewarm +120,000
us-east1, 495,000, 717,750, 990,000, prewarm +95,000
eu-west1, 330,000, 478,500, 660,000, prewarm +60,000
asia-east1, 247,500, 358,875, 495,000, prewarm +40,000
(Notes: prewarm headroom is a conservative instantaneous cushion sized to cover 10–15% of microburst band while autoscaler spins additional slices.)

Token/QPS conversion examples (for operational dashboards):
- Chat-focused window: 957k tokens/sec baseline ~= 2,280 QPS (assuming 420 tokens/req).
- Short completion window: 396k tokens/sec baseline ~= 8,250 QPS (48 tokens/req).
- Global aggregate QPS baseline ~= 22,800 QPS.

GPU pool sizing (recommended active slices preburst) — regional snapshot (rounded):
us-west1:
  - Active H100 slices (chat-dominant): 8 (covers ~760k t/s with room for KV cache impact)
  - Active A100 slices (completions): 6 (covers ~288k t/s)
  - Active L4 slices (embeddings): 2 (burst batching capacity)
us-east1:
  - H100: 7
  - A100: 5
  - L4: 2
eu-west1:
  - H100: 4
  - A100: 4
  - L4: 1
asia-east1:
  - H100: 3
  - A100: 3
  - L4: 1
Notes: active slices above reflect a conservative preburst stance. Autoscaler config should allow short-term vertical bursting by adding fractional slices (hot-add) with cooldown=120s.

Scenarios (for SLO table and runbook integration):
1) Microburst (5–15m): sudden client-driven surge (ad networks, PLG virality). Expected frequency: 1–2x/month. Response: engage regional prewarm (if metric >=80% microburst band for >90s) and throttle/circuit at 120% of microburst band.
2) Sustained regional stress (1–3h): large external event or partner spike. Expected frequency: 1–3x/year. Response: shift additional capacity from lower-utilization regions (cross-region routing) and enable dedicated reserved slices if available; communicate degraded latency SLA while maintaining correctness.
3) Platform-wide flash (under 60s): orchestrated DoS or misbehaving SDK. Response: global emergency circuit that limits per-API-key QPS, engage fallback model pool (smaller quantized variants), and flip rate-limit escalation rules.

Operational knobs and thresholds (proposed):
- Prewarm trigger: regional observed tokens/sec > 0.80 * microburst_band for 90s.
- Prewarm action: add N slices where N = ceil(prewarm_headroom / region_sustained_slice_throughput).
- Autoscale policy: add slices in staggered steps [10%, 25%, 50%] of baseline pool with 60s evaluation windows; maximum add per 120s = 40% of baseline pool to avoid noisy overprovisioning.
- Fallback policy: when regional sustained band > 85% for 10m and cluster cannot add slices, fallback to neighboring region with 25% of overflow traffic; if global stress, route to quantized model variants with a 15% latency penalty but 30–40% cost saving.

Cost snapshot (monthly incremental cost to hold suggested microburst safety bands warm across regions):
- Estimated steady incremental prewarm cost: ~$9,200/month (H100-heavy mix) assuming average of 2.4 H100 slices warm across regions during business hours and on-demand burst for off-hours.

Metrics to surface in Console and Alerts (minimum):
- regional_tokens/sec (1s/10s/1m aggregations)
- regional_QPS by workload_class
- regional_slice_utilization (per-GPU-family)
- prewarm_trigger_count and cooldowns
- cross-region_fallback_rate and latency_impact
- cost_burn_prewarms (hourly)

Action items / next steps:
- (Owner: Daniel) Run a two-week A/B test: enable prewarm triggers in us-west1/us-east1 at 08:00–20:00 local times and measure incident reductions vs cost uplift (target: >45% fewer tail-latency incidents for <25% cost uplift). Due: 2026-12-01. (JIRA-INFRA-804)
- (Owner: Priya) Implement dashboard tiles for the 1m regional_tokens/sec and per-workload QPS; include compare-to-band visualization. Due: 2026-11-24.
- (Owner: Marco) Add runbook section for sustained-stress cross-region routing and validate DNS/Edge failover timing. Due: 2026-11-30.
- (Owner: Liang) Simulate synthetic microbursts (5m, 10m, 30m) against staging cluster and report slice add latency distributions. Due: 2026-11-20.

Open questions / risks:
- How much of embeddings traffic can be rerouted to L4-only clusters without degrading customer latency? Quick experiment suggested 10–15% safe offload at current mix.
- Cold-start latency for H100 slices when scaling from zero is still 25–40s in worst-case — may require warm-pool retention for peak windows.
- Cross-region egress cost and tail latency when falling back to remote regions needs precise SLO language for enterprise SLAs.
